thread.title: Dow rises 173 points before investors turn attention to midterm election returns

author: Mark DeCambre and Chris Matthews
title: Dow rises 173 points before investors turn attention to midterm election returns
text:
U.S. stocks rallied into the close Tuesday, as traders awaited the results of midterm elections that could set the political tone on Wall Street for at least the next two years.
How are the benchmarks performing? The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.68% rose 173.31 points, or 0.68%, to 25,635.01, the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.63% added 17.13 points to reach 2,755.44, a rise of 0.63%, and the Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.64% climbed 0.64%, or 47.11 points, at 7,375.96. The Dow closed at a session high, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended the day just shy of Tuesday’s best levels. On Monday, the Dow had gained 0.8%, and the S&P 500 rose 0.6%, while the Nasdaq Index fell 0.4%.
What’s driving the market? Midterm elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain their grip on the Senate, are under way, and the results could have implications for President Donald Trump’s legislative agenda.
Check out: How traders are thinking about dollar wagers ahead of midterm elections, the Fed
In the final pre-election Wall Street Journal/NBC News poll released Sunday, Democrats held a seven-percentage-point lead on the question of which party should control the next Congress.
The most likely outcome of the elections is political gridlock, which has historically been a positive for investors, but may forestall expectations for infrastructure investments and further deregulation that might help lift shares of financial firms.
Meanwhile, investors were keeping one eye on crude-oil prices CLZ8, -2.11% a day after the Trump administration imposed fresh sanctions aimed at curtailing Iranian oil exports.
Abroad, market participants are also watching developments surrounding U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May‘s tense negotiations with the European Union to exit a longstanding pact with the trade bloc.
Read: Opinion: This is what’s happened to stocks after every midterm election since World War II
Which stocks are in focus? Shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.08% recovered by 1% a day after closing at their lowest level since Aug. 1 and booking the stock’s worst two-day decline since January 2013. Reports that the iPhone maker was scaling back production of a new XR model phone had contributed to its decline.
Shares of Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +0.92% were in focus after reports that the e-commerce giant was set to pick two cities to host its second headquarters , possibly the Long Island City section of Queens in New York and the Crystal City area of Arlington, Va., a Washington suburb. Shares of Amazon rose 0.9% Tuesday.
Under Armour Inc.’s stock UAA, -2.88% fell 2.9%. The company was in the news as the Wall Street Journal reported it had banned the expensing of strip-club outings .
Shares of CVS Health Corp . CVS, +5.71% rose 5.7% after the drugstore and health-care company announced 6.7% same-store-sales growth for the third-quarter on Tuesday morning.
Eli Lilly & Co. LLY, -3.85% finished the day down 3.9% after the pharmaceutical manufacturer reported third-quarter profit and revenue beats and raised its full-year guidance for 2018. The stock is up 25% in 2018.
E.l.f. Beauty Inc . shares ELF, +19.19% rallied 19.2% Tuesday, after its Monday-evening earnings report showed the cosmetics company producing third-quarter projections for revenue and profits that were better than expected. The firm also raised its full-year guidance for 2018.
Shares of Marriott International Inc. MAR, -5.08% tumbled 5.1% after the hotelier reported disappointing sales figures for the third quarter on Tuesday morning.
Mylan NV’s stock MYL, +16.13% rose 16.1%, after the pharmaceutical company announced Monday evening that its profits more than doubled in the third quarter from the year previous.
Shares of Avis Budget Group CAR, -4.90% fell 4.9% on the day, following a Monday earnings report that had the rental-car company falling short of analysts expectations for third-quarter sales and earnings.
Booking Holdings Inc. stock BKNG, +4.19% finished the day up 4.2% Tuesday after the Priceline.com parent reported that it beat analysts estimates for sales and profit in the third quarter.
Mosaic Company shares MOS, +10.61% rose 10.6% following a third-quarter earnings report that showed the company benefiting from rising fertilizer prices .
Archer Daniels Midland Co . ’s stock ADM, -1.60% closed down 1.6% after the food processing and commodities trading firm reported better-than-expected third-quarter sales and earnings Tuesday morning. The stock is up 20.4% on the year.
Shares of Ralph Lauren Corp. RL, -6.59% were off 6.6%, even as the retailer reported revenue and profit beats for the third quarter on Tuesday morning . The stock is up 23.2% on a year-to-date basis.

What data are in focus The Labor Department reported that there were 7 million job openings in the U.S. in September, down from a record 7.3 million in August. The number exceeds the 6.1 million Americans officially classified as unemployed.
What are analysts saying? Charlie Ripley, senior market strategist at Allianz Investment Management, said investors are predicting the Democrats will take the House of Representatives while the Republicans will retain control of the Senate. “We could see a lot more volatility in markets tonight and tomorrow if the result isn’t straight down the fairway,” he told MarketWatch.
If Democrats are able to overcome a deficit in the polls and take the Senate, that could create greater uncertainty, and set up potentially destabilizing political fights over White House oversight and the approval of executive- and judicial-branch appointments, Ripley said. “If we see the Republicans hang on to the House, that could be a boost to markets,” as this result could potentially lead to more aggressive deregulation and tax cuts, he said.
How are other markets trading? Asian markets were mixed Tuesday . European stocks fell Monday, with the Stoxx Europe 600 SXXP, -0.26% down 0.3%.
Oil prices CLZ8, -2.11% fell 1.5%, as gold futures GCZ8, -0.31% edged down 0.4%. The dollar DXY, -0.13% was virtually unchanged.
